summary: The XRD analysis in this paper demonstrates that the synthesized nanocrystals are phase-pure trigonal Cs4PbBr6, with diffraction peaks matching the standard reference pattern for this phase. The data support a successful ligand-mediated transformation from CsPbBr3 to Cs4PbBr6 nanocrystals, as evidenced by the absence of peaks attributable to CsPbBr3 and the close correspondence of observed peak positions to those of bulk Cs4PbBr6.

key_findings.finding: The XRD pattern of the synthesized nanocrystals matches the standard reference for trigonal Cs4PbBr6 (R3̅c), with no evidence of CsPbBr3 or other impurity phases.
The XRD peaks are narrow, indicating good crystallinity of the Cs4PbBr6 nanocrystals.

scientific_interpretation.claim: The ligand-mediated transformation process yields phase-pure Cs4PbBr6 nanocrystals, as indicated by the match between experimental and reference XRD patterns and the absence of secondary phases.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: The experimental XRD pattern shows peaks only at positions corresponding to trigonal Cs4PbBr6, with no additional peaks that would indicate the presence of CsPbBr3 or other phases.

citations.evidence: Experimental XRD pattern matches standard Cs4PbBr6 reference

scientific_interpretation.claim: The narrow XRD peaks suggest that the Cs4PbBr6 nanocrystals possess high crystallinity.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: The analysis notes that the peaks are narrow, which is typically associated with well-crystallized materials.

scientific_interpretation.claim: There is no direct evidence of residual CsPbBr3 phase in the final product based on the XRD data provided.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: No peaks corresponding to CsPbBr3 are reported in the XRD pattern, and the caption/text state that the pattern matches Cs4PbBr6.

citations.evidence: "XRD spectra of trigonal phase Cs4PbBr6 NCs with R3̅ c space group compared to the standard powder diffraction pattern of bulk Cs4PbBr6"

limitations.claim: The XRD analysis does not provide quantitative phase analysis or phase fractions, so trace impurities below the detection limit cannot be ruled out.
No full width at half maximum (FWHM) values are reported, limiting the ability to quantitatively assess crystallite size or strain.
Only one XRD pattern is provided, so the transformation process itself is not directly tracked by XRD (i.e., no before/after comparison of CsPbBr3 and Cs4PbBr6 by XRD).
